## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard the `parseLine` null before `handle`**

`parseLine` returns `null` for blank/whitespace lines by design. `handle(null, …)` then throws a `TypeError` (`frame.kind`), which the outer `try/catch` surfaces as a protocol error and **closes the socket**. A stray blank line (some proxies/servers emit keep-alive newlines; a future server-side change could too) would tear down a healthy session with a scary error banner.

```js
const frame = parseLine(e.data);
if (frame) handle(frame, offered.versions);
```

The loud `catch` stays — it just gets reserved for real protocol failures.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: drop the redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate**

```ts
if (
  kind.startsWith('tool_') &&
  (kind === 'tool_execution_start' || … )
)
```

The explicit kind list already fully determines the set — `startsWith('tool_')` adds a second, wider condition that can never change the outcome (e.g. a hypothetical future `tool_foo` kind passes `startsWith` but fails the inner list, and `tool_pairing_repair` — a known kind with no `toolCallId` requirement — fails `startsWith` semantics either way). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
Dart contract parity looks good. Now run the gates: dart analyze on the new test, dart format check, and the conformance test itself.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1228._

> ℹ️ **12 thread(s) already resolved and excluded from this review.**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The conformance design (golden fixtures pinning the TS client against the Dart server in one gate) is sound and the client mirrors the Dart contract well, but the gate as wired **hangs forever**: bare `node --test` auto-discovers `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`, which starts a server and never exits — reproduced locally on node v22.23.3 (9/9 tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles until killed). CI's sharded `dart test` bin-packs the new hook in, so this blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `node --test` (Dart hook, `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`, and `package.json:9`) discovers `test/mock-serve.mjs` → server keeps the runner alive → CI/job hang with no timeout
- 💡 `Process.runSync` without `timeout`; example renders `parseLine`'s `null` as a fatal protocol error; mock static server serves the whole cwd and can crash on malformed escapes; redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate
- 📦 `sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — add it so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed

**Next Steps**:
1. Name the suite explicitly: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs` in both the Dart hook and `package.json` (or move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/`)
2. Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` call
3. `.gitignore` `sdk/web/dist/`; address the three 💡 inline nits as you see fit

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES (round 2)

**Summary**: Re-reviewed after the round-1 request-changes — **no rework has landed**: same HEAD (`680fd962a`), same +1128/−2 diff, and every flagged line is byte-identical (bare `node --test` at `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22` and `package.json:9`, no `timeout`, unchanged example/mock/client nits). The verified CI-gate hang therefore still blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `node --test` auto-discovers `test/mock-serve.mjs` → server keeps the runner alive → CI/job hang (reproduced round 1 on node v22.23.3; unchanged since)
- 💡 `Process.runSync` timeout, example `parseLine` null-guard, mock static-server confinement / `decodeURIComponent` hardening, redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate — all still open
- 📦 `sdk/web/dist/` still absent from `.gitignore`

**Next Steps**:
1. `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs` in BOTH the Dart hook and `package.json` (or move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/`)
2. Add `timeout:` to the `Process.runSync` call
3. `.gitignore` `sdk/web/dist/`; pick up the four 💡 nits as you see fit

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard the `parseLine` null before `handle`**

`parseLine` returns `null` for blank/whitespace lines by design. `handle(null, …)` then throws a `TypeError` (`frame.kind`), which the outer `try/catch` surfaces as a protocol error and **closes the socket**. A stray blank line (some proxies/servers emit keep-alive newlines; a future server-side change could too) would tear down a healthy session with a scary error banner.

```js
const frame = parseLine(e.data);
if (frame) handle(frame, offered.versions);
```

The loud `catch` stays — it just gets reserved for real protocol failures.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
Dart contract parity looks good. Now run the gates: dart analyze on the new test, dart format check, and the conformance test itself.

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).
- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The conformance design (golden fixtures pinning the TS client against the Dart server in one gate) is sound and the client mirrors the Dart contract well, but the gate as wired **hangs forever**: bare `node --test` auto-discovers `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`, which starts a server and never exits — reproduced locally on node v22.23.3 (9/9 tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles until killed). CI's sharded `dart test` bin-packs the new hook in, so this blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `node --test` (Dart hook, `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`, and `package.json:9`) discovers `test/mock-serve.mjs` → server keeps the runner alive → CI/job hang with no timeout
- 💡 `Process.runSync` without `timeout`; example renders `parseLine`'s `null` as a fatal protocol error; mock static server serves the whole cwd and can crash on malformed escapes; redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate
- 📦 `sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — add it so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed

**Next Steps**:
1. Name the suite explicitly: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs` in both the Dart hook and `package.json` (or move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/`)
2. Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` call
3. `.gitignore` `sdk/web/dist/`; address the three 💡 inline nits as you see fit

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES (round 2)

**Summary**: Re-reviewed after the round-1 request-changes — **no rework has landed**: same HEAD (`680fd962a`), same +1128/−2 diff, and every flagged line is byte-identical (bare `node --test` at `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22` and `package.json:9`, no `timeout`, unchanged example/mock/client nits). The verified CI-gate hang therefore still blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:

- 💡 `Process.runSync` timeout, example `parseLine` null-guard, mock static-server confinement / `decodeURIComponent` hardening, redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate — all still open

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
Dart contract parity looks good. Now run the gates: dart analyze on the new test, dart format check, and the conformance test itself.

Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1228
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1228
- **Title**: feat(1101): Agent Wire Protocol v1 — web reference client (sdk/web), conformance runner, browser example
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1101-wire-protocol` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1150
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T13:59:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T16:36:13Z

## PR Description

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.
- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.
- **`sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`** — dependency-free scripted engine (Node, RFC6455 over raw TCP) for local smoke without fa.
- `sdk/web/README.md` (connect/prompt/approvals, AC6) + `docs/wire-protocol.md` §7 updated to reflect the shipped client.

## Verified

- `node --test` in sdk/web: 9/9 pass; `dist` builds; example script parses.
- `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on the new test; `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` passes (runs the node suite).
- **Browser E2E** (headless Chromium ↔ mock engine): handshake → `connected (protocol v1)`; Cyrillic streamed text rendered mojibake-free (`Привет мир — готово`); tool lifecycle lines; the engine received exactly the golden-shaped frames — `approval_response{approve_once}`, `ask_response{selected:[Postgres]},{freeText:none}`, `secret_response{granted:true,value}` — and the secret value never appears in the page.

## Remaining (slices 3+ of #1101)

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).
- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

Session JSONL untouched, no `lib/` changes (AC7): this slice is purely additive — `sdk/`, one test, one docs line.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard the `parseLine` null before `handle`**

`parseLine` returns `null` for blank/whitespace lines by design. `handle(null, …)` then throws a `TypeError` (`frame.kind`), which the outer `try/catch` surfaces as a protocol error and **closes the socket**. A stray blank line (some proxies/servers emit keep-alive newlines; a future server-side change could too) would tear down a healthy session with a scary error banner.

if (frame) handle(frame, offered.versions);

The loud `catch` stays — it just gets reserved for real protocol failures.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
Dart contract parity looks good. Now run the gates: dart analyze on the new test, dart format check, and the conformance test itself.

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1228
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1228
- **Title**: feat(1101): Agent Wire Protocol v1 — web reference client (sdk/web), conformance runner, browser example
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1101-wire-protocol` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1150
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T13:59:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T16:36:13Z

## PR Description

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.
- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.
- **`sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`** — dependency-free scripted engine (Node, RFC6455 over raw TCP) for local smoke without fa.
- `sdk/web/README.md` (connect/prompt/approvals, AC6) + `docs/wire-protocol.md` §7 updated to reflect the shipped client.

## Verified

- `node --test` in sdk/web: 9/9 pass; `dist` builds; example script parses.
- `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on the new test; `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` passes (runs the node suite).
- **Browser E2E** (headless Chromium ↔ mock engine): handshake → `connected (protocol v1)`; Cyrillic streamed text rendered mojibake-free (`Привет мир — готово`); tool lifecycle lines; the engine received exactly the golden-shaped frames — `approval_response{approve_once}`, `ask_response{selected:[Postgres]},{freeText:none}`, `secret_response{granted:true,value}` — and the secret value never appears in the page.

## Remaining (slices 3+ of #1101)

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).
- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

Session JSONL untouched, no `lib/` changes (AC7): this slice is purely additive — `sdk/`, one test, one docs line.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1228._

> ℹ️ **12 thread(s) already resolved and excluded from this review.**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 13

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The conformance design (golden fixtures pinning the TS client against the Dart server in one gate) is sound and the client mirrors the Dart contract well, but the gate as wired **hangs forever**: bare `node --test` auto-discovers `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`, which starts a server and never exits — reproduced locally on node v22.23.3 (9/9 tests pass in ~85 ms, then the runner idles until killed). CI's sharded `dart test` bin-packs the new hook in, so this blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `node --test` (Dart hook, `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22`, and `package.json:9`) discovers `test/mock-serve.mjs` → server keeps the runner alive → CI/job hang with no timeout
- 💡 `Process.runSync` without `timeout`; example renders `parseLine`'s `null` as a fatal protocol error; mock static server serves the whole cwd and can crash on malformed escapes; redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate
- 📦 `sdk/web/dist/` (build output) is not in `.gitignore` — add it so the type-stripped bundle is never accidentally committed

**Next Steps**:
1. Name the suite explicitly: `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs` in both the Dart hook and `package.json` (or move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/`)
2. Add a `timeout` to the `Process.runSync` call
3. `.gitignore` `sdk/web/dist/`; address the three 💡 inline nits as you see fit

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES (round 2)

**Summary**: Re-reviewed after the round-1 request-changes — **no rework has landed**: same HEAD (`680fd962a`), same +1128/−2 diff, and every flagged line is byte-identical (bare `node --test` at `web_client_conformance_test.dart:22` and `package.json:9`, no `timeout`, unchanged example/mock/client nits). The verified CI-gate hang therefore still blocks merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `node --test` auto-discovers `test/mock-serve.mjs` → server keeps the runner alive → CI/job hang (reproduced round 1 on node v22.23.3; unchanged since)
- 💡 `Process.runSync` timeout, example `parseLine` null-guard, mock static-server confinement / `decodeURIComponent` hardening, redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate — all still open
- 📦 `sdk/web/dist/` still absent from `.gitignore`

**Next Steps**:
1. `node --test test/conformance.test.mjs` in BOTH the Dart hook and `package.json` (or move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/`)
2. Add `timeout:` to the `Process.runSync` call
3. `.gitignore` `sdk/web/dist/`; pick up the four 💡 nits as you see fit

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). Killing the mock child lets the runner finish. Since `Process.runSync` has no `timeout`, `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` hangs the same way — the PR's own "Verified" claim cannot reproduce under bare `node --test`, and CI's sharded `dart test` (unknown files are bin-packed into shards) will burn the full job timeout.

Fix by naming the suite explicitly (and keep the loud-failure contract):

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `npm test` hangs the same way — scope the test glob**

`node --test` with no arguments applies node's default discovery patterns, which include all `.js`/`.mjs` files under `**/test/**` — so this script also executes `test/mock-serve.mjs`. The mock starts a server on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it; the runner then never exits (verified: process alive 15+ min after the 9/9 conformance pass). The README tells users to run `npm test`, so anyone following the docs hits the hang.

```json
"test": "node --test test/conformance.test.mjs"
```

(The browser-ext workflow already follows this discipline: `node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs` — see the comment in `.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml` about not relying on bare discovery.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: add a `timeout` to the node invocation**

`Process.runSync` without `timeout` waits forever. Once the discovery hang above is fixed a stuck/hung node (loaded CI runner, future regression) would still block the Dart suite until the outer CI step times out, losing the loud, localized failure this test is designed to produce. A bounded wait keeps the failure actionable:

```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
  timeout: const Duration(seconds: 120),
);
```

(Adjust the budget to a bit above the suite's worst-case CI runtime; today it finishes in well under a second.)

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: guard the `parseLine` null before `handle`**

`parseLine` returns `null` for blank/whitespace lines by design. `handle(null, …)` then throws a `TypeError` (`frame.kind`), which the outer `try/catch` surfaces as a protocol error and **closes the socket**. A stray blank line (some proxies/servers emit keep-alive newlines; a future server-side change could too) would tear down a healthy session with a scary error banner.

```js
const frame = parseLine(e.data);
if (frame) handle(frame, offered.versions);
```

The loud `catch` stays — it just gets reserved for real protocol failures.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: confine the static server to its doc root (and harden the URL decode)**

Two robustness nits in the mock's HTTP leg, worth a line each since this file is also a reference readers copy from:

1. **Serves the whole process cwd.** After `normalize` + leading-slash strip the path is clamped to cwd, so any file under `sdk/web` is fetchable — `/package.json`, `/src/wire-client.ts`, `/test/conformance.test.mjs`. It's loopback-only and a dev mock, so impact is low, but the README advertises "serves `example/`". Resolve against an explicit root (`path.resolve(exampleDir, path)`) and reject results that don't start with it.

2. **`decodeURIComponent` can throw.** A malformed escape (`GET /%zz`) makes it throw `URIError`; inside the `async` handler that becomes an unhandled rejection, which under node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` **crashes the whole mock**. Wrap the decode in the same try/catch that already produces the 404.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-04):

💡 **SUGGESTION: drop the redundant `startsWith('tool_')` predicate**

```ts
if (
  kind.startsWith('tool_') &&
  (kind === 'tool_execution_start' || … )
)
```

The explicit kind list already fully determines the set — `startsWith('tool_')` adds a second, wider condition that can never change the outcome (e.g. a hypothetical future `tool_foo` kind passes `startsWith` but fails the inner list, and `tool_pairing_repair` — a known kind with no `toolCallId` requirement — fails `startsWith` semantics either way). # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into

    outputs:

      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}

      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. ## PR Description

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:
  - handshake: `helloFrame` / `acceptWelcome` / `negotiate` — max-overlap negotiation, LOUD `WireVersionError` on no overlap (AC2 semantics)
  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.
- **CI hook** `test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` — `dart test` invokes `node --test`, so the Dart server and the TS client drift-proof each other in the existing CI gate (AC4/UT-3); loud failure when node is missing.
- **Browser example** `sdk/web/example/index.html` — vanilla-JS chat over WebSocket to `fa wire-serve`: handshake, prompt/steer/abort, streamed text, tool lifecycle, approval/ask/secret answers via dialogs, graceful `unknown_event`; secrets sent but never rendered. `build.mjs` (node type-stripping) emits `dist/` — no toolchain, no deps.
- **`sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`** — dependency-free scripted engine (Node, RFC6455 over raw TCP) for local smoke without fa.
- `sdk/web/README.md` (connect/prompt/approvals, AC6) + `docs/wire-protocol.md` §7 updated to reflect the shipped client.

## Verified

- `node --test` in sdk/web: 9/9 pass; `dist` builds; example script parses.
- `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on the new test; `dart test test/wire/web_client_conformance_test.dart` passes (runs the node suite).
- **Browser E2E** (headless Chromium ↔ mock engine): handshake → `connected (protocol v1)`; Cyrillic streamed text rendered mojibake-free (`Привет мир — готово`); tool lifecycle lines; the engine received exactly the golden-shaped frames — `approval_response{approve_once}`, `ask_response{selected:[Postgres]},{freeText:none}`, `secret_response{granted:true,value}` — and the secret value never appears in the page.

## Remaining (slices 3+ of #1101)

- `sdk/ios`, `sdk/android`, `sdk/macos`, `sdk/rn` clients + their conformance runners (same fixture corpus).
- EMB-0/1/2 embedded-runtime spikes (OQ1a) and the shared scripted-scenario fixture divergence guard.
- Downgrade filter (E5) gets real teeth when a second live version exists; today v1 is the only live version by design.

Session JSONL untouched, no `lib/` changes (AC7): this slice is purely additive — `sdk/`, one test, one docs line.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `node --test` never exits — the CI conformance gate hangs until job timeout**

This test invokes bare `node --test` with `workingDirectory: 'sdk/web'`. Node's default test-file discovery (node >= 22) matches **every** `*.js`/`*.mjs` file under any `test/` directory — including `sdk/web/test/mock-serve.mjs`. That file is not a test: its top level starts an HTTP + WebSocket server listening on `127.0.0.1:8091` and never closes it, so the spawned subprocess keeps its event loop alive forever and the runner never completes.

Reproduced on this checkout (node v22.23.3): `cd sdk/web && node --test` — all 9 conformance tests pass in ~85 ms, then the process hangs indefinitely (still alive after 15+ minutes; `ps` shows `node test/mock-serve.mjs` as a runner child). ```dart
result = Process.runSync(
  'node',
  ['--test', 'test/conformance.test.mjs'],
  workingDirectory: 'sdk/web',
);
```

Alternatively move `mock-serve.mjs` out of `test/` (e.g. `example/` or `scripts/`) so discovery can't pick it up — but naming the file is the robust fix, because any future non-test helper dropped into `test/` would reintroduce the hang.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
Dart contract parity looks good. Now run the gates: dart analyze on the new test, dart format check, and the conformance test itself.

changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: changes
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false

## PR Description

Part of #1101 (slice 2: the `sdk/` reference-client layer; slice 1 landed the schema, versioning, golden fixtures, and in-process adapter).

## Delivered

- **`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`** — zero-dependency TypeScript reference client mirroring `lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart`:

  - all 7 command builders (`prompt`, `steer`, `abort`, `approval_response`, `ask_response`, `secret_response`, `session_control`) + `encodeUnknownEvent`, canonical shapes
  - `decodeEvent`: known / request / unknown classification, unknown-field tolerance (additive rule), unknown-kind → `unknown_event` passthrough (E3), loud version gate
  - NDJSON framing (`frameLine`/`parseLine`, one object per line — NOT JSONP), `messageText` partial-first render helper
  - E4 secrets: `isSecretField` registry + `redactForLog` (frame-kind-labeled `[REDACTED:…]`, `rawBody` anywhere)
- **Conformance runner** `sdk/web/test/conformance.test.mjs` (node:test, 9 tests): parses EVERY golden event fixture with the pinned classification, reproduces EVERY pinned command frame from the semantic payload, handshake/negotiation cases, version gate, NDJSON incl. Cyrillic UTF-8, E4 redaction.
